answer: Yes. Dr. Amsel has the depth appropriate to the protagonist: intellectual curiosity, dry humor, protectiveness toward the recordings, and a changing relationship to institutional uncertainty. Supporting characters have distinct, proportionate identities—Mrs. Blythe’s meticulous recordkeeping and wit, Dr. Solberg’s determined adaptation, and Ms. Farrow’s bureaucratic language and persistence. Even briefly appearing characters contribute to the department’s shared experience without needing elaborate personal arcs.
